article_blocks.text: Strain Type: Sativa-leaning hybrid
Genetics: Strawberry Cough × The White
Breeder: Connoisseur Genetics
THC Content: 18-20% range
CBD Content: Generally low
Terpene Profile: myrcene , beta-caryophyllene , pinene
Primary Flavors: Strawberry, sweet berry, pine, earth
Flowering Time (Indoor): 9–10 weeks
Outdoor Harvest Time: October
Indoor Yield: Medium to high
Outdoor Yield: Medium to high
Grow Difficulty: Moderate

Some cannabis strains acquire dessert names after growers notice a vague sweetness in the finished flower. Strawberries and Cream is considerably less abstract. At its best, the cultivar produces an unmistakable fresh-strawberry character layered over pine, earthy hash, and a softer sweetness that makes the name seem unusually appropriate. Connoisseur Genetics created this version by crossing Strawberry Cough with The White, combining one parent famous for aromatic fruit and energetic cerebral effects with another prized for enormous resin production.

The result is a sativa-leaning hybrid that looks substantially frostier and more compact than its Strawberry Cough ancestry might suggest. Its appeal extends beyond flavor: the strain offers an animated mental lift followed by a gradual loosening of physical tension, while the plant itself responds well to training and can produce medium-to-heavy harvests. Because another major breeder later released a completely different cultivar under the Strawberries and Cream name, identifying the breeder is essential. The strain discussed here is the Connoisseur Genetics Strawberry Cough × The White version.
Genetics and Lineage

Connoisseur Genetics lists the cross plainly as Strawberry Cough × The White. Strawberry Cough supplies the expressive side of the genetic equation. The famous cultivar is traditionally associated with Strawberry Fields and Haze ancestry, and its reputation rests on fresh strawberry aromatics, vigorous sativa-oriented growth, and an effect that tends to emphasize mood, sociability, and cerebral stimulation. Incorporating it into a cross can introduce significant stretch and longer flowering behavior, but it also provides the bright fruit character that defines Strawberries and Cream. The White approaches cannabis breeding from a very different direction. This clone-only American cultivar became respected less for an extravagant aroma than for its exceptional frost, dense flower development, and potency. Mature flowers can appear almost powdered with resin, which explains the name.

Bringing those parents together created a plant capable of carrying Strawberry Cough’s aromatic personality on a framework strengthened by The White. The buds commonly develop a heavy layer of trichomes, while the floral scent becomes deeper than straight strawberry. Pine, hash, earth, and resinous spice fill out the background. Connoisseur Genetics specifically describes the cultivar as having strawberry aroma and taste surrounded by full-bodied pine and hash undertones, while also highlighting its suitability for resin and hash production. The plant shows moderate stretch instead of the more aggressive vertical expansion possible in some Haze-heavy marijuana genetics, giving cultivators more control over final height.

Confusion surrounding the name deserves clarification. Exotic Genetix also bred a Strawberries & Cream, but that plant is genetically unrelated to this one. Exotic’s cultivar comes from Strawberry Jelly × Cookies & Cream F2, whereas the Connoisseur Genetics release is Strawberry Cough × The White. Both may appear on dispensary menus simply as “Strawberries and Cream,” so the name alone cannot establish ancestry.
Effects and Experience

The initial phase tends to reflect Strawberry Cough more strongly than The White. Instead of moving immediately toward sedation, the experience can begin with a noticeable sharpening of mood and perception. Thoughts may feel more fluid, conversation more inviting, and mundane tasks somewhat easier to engage with. Creative activities, music, casual social situations, or an unhurried afternoon can pair naturally with the cultivar because the cerebral stimulation generally arrives with an upbeat quality rather than overwhelming physical heaviness. Some batches can feel distinctly energetic during the first hour, particularly when consumed at lower amounts.

Physical relaxation usually becomes easier to notice after the cerebral peak has settled. Rather than abruptly switching into couch-lock, the weed tends to soften muscle tension and produce a comfortable body calm while leaving much of the mental uplift intact. That progression makes Strawberries and Cream more flexible than a heavily sedating indica. A smaller serving can remain suitable for daytime or early evening, whereas a larger amount may produce a slower, dreamier experience as The White’s potency becomes more prominent. Appetite stimulation is also possible once the initial mental energy begins to level out.

Potency should not be underestimated simply because the flavor is sweet. Modern examples carrying authentic genetics can reach substantial THC levels, and individual plants differ according to phenotype, cultivation environment, and harvest timing. Excessive consumption may produce dry mouth, dry eyes, dizziness, racing thoughts, or temporary anxiety, particularly in people who are sensitive to THC or stimulating cannabis varieties. Anyone unfamiliar with the strain is better served by judging a tested batch on its cannabinoid content rather than relying on a generalized strain average.
Medical Benefits

The combination of mental uplift and gradual body relaxation helps explain why some medical marijuana consumers gravitate toward this cultivar. During the first portion of the experience, its brighter cerebral quality may be attractive to people using cannabis while dealing with stress, low mood, or mental fatigue. Unlike marijuana that immediately promotes sleepiness, Strawberries and Cream may allow a patient to remain conversational and engaged while experiencing a change in mood and physical tension.

As the experience develops, the relaxing component may be useful for people seeking relief from minor aches, muscle tightness, or general physical discomfort. Appetite may increase as well, making the cultivar potentially appealing to some individuals who struggle with reduced hunger. The relatively balanced transition between mind and body also means the strain may suit people who find purely stimulating sativas too edgy but do not want the pronounced lethargy associated with heavier nighttime weed.

These possible applications are based on cannabis pharmacology and patterns of consumer experience rather than clinical trials performed specifically on Strawberries and Cream. A strain name is not a medical treatment, and cannabinoid chemistry can vary substantially between growers. Patients should pay closer attention to the tested THC, CBD, and terpene content of the actual flower they are purchasing. People taking prescription medications, managing serious medical conditions, or using cannabis regularly for symptom control should discuss marijuana use with a healthcare professional familiar with their individual circumstances.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Fresh strawberry is the calling card, but describing this cultivar as simply “berry-flavored” misses much of what makes it interesting. Properly cured flowers can open with a bright red-fruit aroma reminiscent of ripe strawberries, strawberry preserves, or lightly tart berry candy. Beneath that sweetness sits a considerably darker layer of pine needles, dry earth, hash, and resin. Connoisseur Genetics specifically emphasized the strawberry, pine, and hash combination when describing the original release, and those contrasting elements prevent the flower from becoming sugary or one-dimensional.

Breaking apart a dense bud usually intensifies the herbal side. Pine may become sharper while earth and spice move forward, and some phenotypes reveal a faint woody or floral character. The flavor often begins sweeter than the aroma suggests. Strawberry arrives early on the palate, followed by resinous pine and an earthy, hash-like finish. A well-grown specimen can retain fruit through the exhale rather than losing it immediately to generic cannabis smoke, which is one reason the strain developed a reputation as connoisseur flower.

Terpene composition is less standardized than strain descriptions often imply. Myrcene, caryophyllene, pinene, and limonene are plausible and commonly encountered components in commercial material, but Connoisseur Genetics does not define the cultivar through a fixed laboratory terpene percentage. Growing medium, temperature, light intensity, harvest maturity, drying, and storage can all shift the finished aromatic profile. A batch that smells intensely of strawberries and pine may therefore have a noticeably different terpene ratio from another authentic plant expressing more hash, earth, or spice.
Growing Information

Connoisseur Genetics gives Strawberries and Cream an indoor flowering period of approximately nine to ten weeks and describes yield as medium to high. The breeder also notes medium stretch and specifically recommends training or topping when the goal is increased production. Those characteristics make the plant more manageable than its Strawberry Cough heritage might suggest. Growers can expect enough vertical movement after flowering begins to require planning, but the plant generally responds well when the canopy is shaped before branches become rigid with mature flowers.

Topping early can encourage several productive leaders instead of allowing one dominant central stem to control the canopy. Low-stress training can further spread those branches, helping light reach flowering sites lower on the plant. Resin production is one of its strongest horticultural features. The White ancestry contributes heavy trichome development, and Connoisseur Genetics specifically promoted this cultivar as a good candidate for hash production. Dense, frosted flowers can become visually impressive late in bloom, with orange pistils standing against dark green foliage and a pale resin coating.

Outdoor growers should plan around the nine-to-ten-week bloom period, which generally places Northern Hemisphere harvest during October. A reasonably dry autumn is helpful because mature flowers can become dense enough to trap moisture. Air circulation is especially important as buds gain weight. The plant does not demand expert-level technique, but cultivators who manage its stretch, create an open canopy, and protect late flowers from prolonged humidity are likely to see considerably better results than growers who leave it entirely untrained.
FAQ
What strain is Strawberries and Cream?

The Connoisseur Genetics version of Strawberries and Cream is a sativa-leaning hybrid created from Strawberry Cough × The White. It combines strong strawberry aromatics and cerebral stimulation with heavy resin production and a gradually relaxing body effect.
Is Strawberries and Cream indica or sativa?

It is generally considered a sativa-leaning hybrid. Strawberry Cough contributes much of the cerebral energy and fruit character, while The White adds density, potency, resin, and a more physically relaxing component.
What does Strawberries and Cream taste like?

The dominant flavor is sweet strawberry, but the profile is more complex than the name suggests. Pine, hash, earth, herbs, and light spice appear behind the fruit, especially on the exhale. Connoisseur Genetics specifically describes the original cultivar as combining strawberry with full-bodied pine and hash undertones.
How long does Strawberries and Cream take to flower?

Connoisseur Genetics lists an indoor flowering period of approximately nine to ten weeks. The plant has moderate stretch and responds well to topping and training, which can help growers create a more productive canopy.
Are there different Strawberries and Cream strains?

Yes. This is one of the most important details surrounding the name. Connoisseur Genetics bred Strawberry Cough × The White, while Exotic Genetix produced a separate Strawberries & Cream from Strawberry Jelly × Cookies & Cream F2. The plants are different cultivars despite sharing essentially the same name.
Final Thoughts on Strawberries and Cream

Strawberries and Cream demonstrates what can happen when a highly aromatic cannabis parent is paired with genetics chosen primarily for resin and flower quality. Strawberry Cough brings the unmistakable fruit character, mental brightness, and sativa influence; The White contributes frost, density, potency, and enough physical weight to prevent the experience from feeling purely stimulating. The finished hybrid does not simply taste sweet. Pine, earth, hash, and resin provide contrast underneath the strawberry aroma, giving well-cured flowers a more mature and layered profile than the dessert-style name might imply.

Growers have equally practical reasons to appreciate the cultivar. A nine-to-ten-week flowering cycle is manageable for a sativa-leaning hybrid, medium stretch can be controlled with training, and the plant’s heavy trichome production gives the finished buds considerable visual appeal. Its ability to respond positively to topping also provides room for cultivators to shape the plant according to available space rather than accommodating an unruly natural structure.

The one complication is identity. “Strawberries and Cream” does not describe a single universally agreed-upon genetic line, and the Exotic Genetix version has become prominent enough that dispensary labels can be misleading. For the cultivar documented here, the defining information is simple: Connoisseur Genetics, Strawberry Cough × The White. With that distinction established, Strawberries and Cream stands as a flavorful, resin-heavy hybrid that successfully combines classic strawberry cannabis aromatics with the frosted potency of one of America’s better-known clone-only breeding plants.
